preregistration.acquisition_start_criterion: acquisition starts when the first schema-valid A2 replica observation is retained for inspection

origin_disclosure.use_limit: the committed diagnosis, reviews, audit, and retained A1 run-12 bundle are exploratory design and pre-acquisition analyzer dry-run inputs only; they are never A2 evidence and cannot satisfy any A2 derivation, holdout, or decision predicate

preregistration.amendment_rule: after the first acquisition starts, any change requires a new experiment id, plan file, and provenance entry

question: Can separately delimited record-level models explain and predict the observed global and per-table allocation-map transitions in three fresh Jet 3 databases?

replicas.acquisition_independence: each replica is created, mutated, closed, captured, validated, and uploaded by a separate matrix job that reads no other replica and shares no database, page store, output directory, or mutable state
replicas.fan_in_rule: the fan-in analyzer first validates only replica 1 and 2 artifacts, derives and persists every layered candidate set, records its SHA-256, and closes those inputs. Only after that freeze, a separate holdout structural-validation process validates replica 3 and writes a bounded pass/fail receipt plus artifact hash without exposing page bytes to the analyzer; the analyzer may then open replica 3 and evaluate every frozen layer without refit, candidate addition, deletion, relaxation, or reinterpretation
replicas.environment_identity_rule: each matrix job produces its own environment document and SHA-256. Across replicas, DAO prog id, provider CLSID and binary SHA-256, x86 process architecture, and PowerShell major must match exactly; Windows image and Python patch version may differ only within the plan bindings and are recorded per replica

row_algorithm.id: positive one-based monotonically increasing signed 32-bit integer within each logical role; deleted Id values are reinserted unchanged
row_algorithm.payload: repeat the ASCII seed A2|<role>|<Id as ten zero-padded decimal digits>| and truncate to exactly 240 characters
row_algorithm.rolling_sha256: one SHA-256 stream over each row encoded as Id signed little-endian 32-bit, Payload UTF-8 byte length unsigned little-endian 16-bit, then Payload ASCII bytes
row_algorithm.delete_rule: at L_DELETE_ALL delete every row from L in Id order so its data pages are eligible to become free; at L_REINSERT_SAME reinsert the exact same Id values and payload bytes
row_algorithm.reread_requirement: after every checkpoint, DAO must return the exact expected count and rolling SHA-256 for every extant table

checkpoint_design.d_growth_rule: D_GROW_0128 is the first closed-file state after a fixed 32-row batch whose page count is at least the post-create D baseline plus 128; record the exact achieved D row count N and overshoot without retuning
checkpoint_design.d_regrowth_rule: after D_DROP, recreate the same empty D definition and capture D_RECREATE_EMPTY; from that closed-file post-recreate baseline, insert fixed 32-row batches until file pages are at least baseline plus 128, record the achieved row count and overshoot, and capture D_REGROW_0128. The D_REGROW_0128 page count must be strictly greater than D_GROW_0128; no row-count replay, truncation, page-count equality, or byte equality is assumed
checkpoint_design.relative_growth_rule: each L_REL or H_REL checkpoint is the first closed-file state after a fixed 32-row batch whose page count is at least that table's post-create baseline plus the named target; record overshoot and do not retune
checkpoint_design.absolute_growth_rule: each P_ABS checkpoint is the first closed-file state after a fixed 32-row batch whose total file page count is at least the named target; record overshoot and do not retune
checkpoint_design.schedule_minimization_basis: exploratory A1 run-12 page-1 transitions justified retaining the L targets that span each coarse regime, the first fine transition, the 1024 and 1088 boundary probes, every P checkpoint needed to locate rather than assume the inline-to-indirect conversion, and H 64 plus 896-to-904. H_REL_0064 forces the slot-0 predictions of slot-relative and referenced-page-relative base candidates to differ; the other fine and later H points are excluded because they add repeated snapshots without adding a required A2 predicate

page_capture.checkpoint_representation: ordered physical-page SHA-256 values from page zero through the final page

record_candidate_procedure.boundary_source: after page qualification, enumerate every half-open interval [start,end) from the fixed byte-boundary set {0,1,...,2048}, with 0 <= start < end <= 2048; boundaries are never inferred from the minimum or maximum changed byte
record_candidate_procedure.candidate_page_space: the finite page space is the union of every physical page index observed at any checkpoint in either derivation replica; absence is an explicit state and no all-checkpoint intersection or E0R-present filter is permitted
record_candidate_procedure.global_page_qualification: before any interval enumeration, qualify a global page using hashes only: its explicit presence/hash state must differ across E0 to D_GROW_0128 and across D_GROW_0128 to D_DROP. Absence is a distinct state, and absence at both endpoints is equality. More than 12 qualifying pages is a resource_bound_breach
record_candidate_procedure.tdef_page_qualification: before any interval enumeration, qualify a TDEF page using hashes only: it must be present at E0, because the table-definition record exists when the empty tables are created; its explicit presence/hash state must differ on at least one declared L or H growth transition and on both L_REL_1280 to L_DELETE_ALL and L_DELETE_ALL to L_REINSERT_SAME. Absence is a distinct state, and absence at both endpoints is equality. More than 12 qualifying pages is a resource_bound_breach
record_candidate_procedure.global_record_end_resolution: for intervals on one qualified page that share a start and decode the same D relation, retain only the page-terminal interval ending at 2048 when every byte after the last D-flipped byte through byte 2047 is zero at every D checkpoint and the zero suffix is at least 16 bytes long; all shorter equivalent ends are rejected. If the byte property is absent or more than one start survives, emit global_record_end_not_resolved or multiple_global_record_boundaries_survive respectively
record_candidate_procedure.tdef_record_resolution: a TDEF interval must be inclusion-minimal while wholly containing the two distinct transition-selective four-byte pointer windows plus one byte that is stable at every checkpoint on each available side; extending into a byte that changes outside either pointer signature invalidates the interval. Zero or multiple minimal intervals have distinct outcomes
record_candidate_procedure.structural_exclusion_rule: apply identically on every page: a global-map field may change only with the D set relation or declared post-delimitation global growth transitions; a growth-pointer window must be stable on D, churn, and idle transitions; a churn-pointer window must be stable on D, growth, and idle transitions. Any byte changing outside its field signature rejects that field or window. Bytes are never classified as headers by page number or offset: a byte is eligible only when it satisfies the same field signature, and otherwise is excluded without assigning header meaning. No page number or byte offset is privileged or blacklisted
record_candidate_procedure.prefix_sum_work_model: for each qualified page and transition class, build fixed 2049-entry prefix sums over byte predicates once, charging one work unit per prefix cell. Test each interval, polarity, zero-suffix closure, and transition-selectivity property with O(1) prefix-difference queries; charge at most eight work units per enumerated interval across both sub-model searches and never scan interval length
record_candidate_procedure.multiple_records_on_one_page: enumerate and score overlapping intervals independently, then apply the preregistered global page-terminal or TDEF inclusion-minimal byte-property resolution; deterministic replica agreement cannot replace uniqueness

inline_boundary_procedure.subject: the D-delimited global_map record after its page, start, and end are frozen
inline_boundary_procedure.candidate_source: enumerate every byte boundary b in the fixed set {global_map.start+5,...,global_map.end}; do not derive candidates from the last nonzero byte, fill level, or an anchor checkpoint
inline_boundary_procedure.survival_rule: evaluate each b against every checkpoint in transition_coverage.inline_to_indirect_conversion_window on the frozen global_map record: bytes and bits before b must explain the complete declared allocation sequence, windows at or after b must satisfy declared global-map pointer and type-1 rules, and bytes classified as unused suffix must be zero at every applicable checkpoint
inline_boundary_procedure.ambiguity_rule: zero surviving boundaries emits no_inline_boundary_candidate and more than one emits multiple_inline_boundary_candidates; deterministic agreement across replicas cannot rescue a boundary selected from anchor fill

hypotheses.bit_polarity_rule: evaluate both polarities on the D-delimited global_map record only. Let G be in_use(D_GROW_0128) minus in_use(E0); the selected polarity is the unique value for which G is nonempty, every G page is not in use after D_DROP, every G page is in use at D_REGROW_0128, and regrowth adds at least one page beyond first growth. Zero or two values are named global-map no-outcomes
hypotheses.polarity_cross_check: after D alone freezes polarity, L/P/H growth on the same global_map record must flip newly allocated pages from not-in-use to in-use under that polarity, regardless of raw bit direction. Disagreement emits growth_polarity_disagreement for the global conversion layer but never retroactively changes D polarity or the global record
hypotheses.global_map_record_predicate: decode each candidate interval as represented page sets under each polarity and apply the D-only allocation, release, reallocation, and additional-regrowth relation. D_DROP need not shrink the file, and no byte, record, or page equality between checkpoints is a predicate
hypotheses.global_map_search: use only E0, D_GROW_0128, D_DROP, D_RECREATE_EMPTY, and D_REGROW_0128 to qualify and delimit the global_map record. After its page and boundaries are frozen, evaluate conversion, slot activation, inline boundary, polarity agreement, and extended-map bases on that same record with the preregistered L/P/H transitions
hypotheses.tdef_record_search: search a separate tdef record only for the growth-only and churn-only pointer windows. The tdef record carries no conversion, slot-activation, inline-boundary, bit-polarity, or extended-base hypothesis
hypotheses.growth_only_pointer_predicate: inside the tdef record, a decoded reference changes on one or more declared L or H growth transitions, resolves to a page in candidate_page_space whose byte-zero tag is 0x05 when active, and is unchanged across L_REL_1280, L_DELETE_ALL, and L_REINSERT_SAME
hypotheses.delete_reinsert_only_pointer_predicate: inside the tdef record, a decoded reference is stable through declared L growth, differs at L_DELETE_ALL, returns exactly at L_REINSERT_SAME, and resolves to a page in candidate_page_space whose byte-zero tag is 0x05 whenever active. Enable only if L_REL_1280 has a nonempty L data page and L_DELETE_ALL DAO-rereads zero rows, thereby emptying a formerly nonempty page; otherwise report legacy_churn_precondition_not_met for the tdef layer
hypotheses.pointer_pair_rule: growth-only and delete/reinsert-only windows must be distinct, use one declared layout, lie wholly inside the same tdef interval, and satisfy the predicates in both derivation replicas before holdout access
hypotheses.inline_extent_rule: one exact boundary inside the frozen global_map record must agree across derivation replicas, explain every applicable transition across the full conversion window, and satisfy the all-checkpoint suffix rule; anchor fill is never a boundary source
hypotheses.type1_conversion_predicate: classify every checkpoint in transition_coverage.inline_to_indirect_conversion_window on the frozen global_map record, derive the earliest valid indirect checkpoint after at least one valid inline predecessor, require exactly one monotone transition, and do not require conversion by any phase boundary
hypotheses.type1_rule: slot activation at conversion is a free parameter 0, 1, or 2. A decisive conversion layer requires at least one active reference at conversion and exactly two active references by H_REL_0904; one or two at conversion are valid, zero emits no_active_slot_at_conversion, and a final count other than two emits final_slot_activation_not_two
hypotheses.pointer_validity_rule: for global-map slots and tdef pointers, require tag and in-range validity only at transition_coverage.pointer_validity_checkpoints at or after the applicable activation checkpoint and only for nonzero references; preactivation zero values and checkpoints outside that set are not failures
hypotheses.extended_base_rule: evaluate the preregistered formulas on the frozen global_map record using actual flip direction. H_REL_0064 is the planned slot-0 discriminator, but failure to produce a discriminating flip yields insufficient_base_discrimination only for the extended_base layer; it cannot erase a decisive global record, conversion layer, or tdef pointer layer. No formula may be added after acquisition

analyzer_dry_run_contract.dispatch_gate: before any A2 matrix job is dispatched, both dry-run modes and the decisive-report validator case must produce schema-valid pass reports; every required assertion must be present, inputs and fixtures must match recorded hashes, no holdout artifact may be opened, and the additive provenance disclosure must be committed and pushed. Any failure leaves acquisition BLOCKED

retained_a1_input.holdout_access: replicas 1 and 2 only; replica 3 and every holdout artifact are excluded and must not be opened
retained_a1_input.schedule_arithmetic_assertion: assert first D baseline 23 to 151, D_DROP remains 151, post-recreate baseline 151 to 279, 32-row batches and recorded overshoot, and alternating L deletion changes page count by +1 without satisfying the A2 full-delete premise
retained_a1_input.candidate_bound_assertion: using page hashes before interval reads, assert the observed run-12 D-qualified page count is exactly 10, each submodel is below 12 qualified pages, enumerated intervals are no more than 50,356,224 combined, prefix construction plus O(1) interval queries remains below 500,000,000 work units, and no more than 55 blobs are opened
retained_a1_input.record_end_assertion: apply the page-terminal all-D-zero suffix property and assert one global record survivor with at least 16 zero bytes of slack after the last D-flipped byte; shorter equivalent ends must be rejected. Assert that run-12 control-changing bytes outside a field signature cannot become global-map fields or TDEF pointer windows, without naming or blacklisting their offsets
retained_a1_input.required_behavior: complete the explicit projection, select set_means_not_in_use uniquely from D alone, check L/H agreement on the frozen global record, report legacy_projection_complete_with_tdef_churn_not_applicable by name, retain layered calibration results, and emit no A2 scientific evidence

synthetic_input.generation_rule: parse checkpoint_design, tables.row_algorithm, record_candidate_procedure, and bounds from this exact plan and derive every checkpoint, baseline, target, 32-row batch, overshoot, page and row count, page state, qualified-page count, prefix sum, record candidate, and work unit with the worker and analyzer arithmetic; hand-typed counts and inherited A1 schedules are forbidden

free_parameters.conversion_ordinal: for the input schedule, generate every noninitial ordinal plus never: A1 legacy ordinals 1..70 plus never and A2 ordinals 1..24 plus never

synthetic_input.run12_calibration_case: on the global_map fixture, generate source conversion ordinal 40, checkpoint P_ABS_16480, A2 ordinal 20, two active slots, set_means_not_in_use because growth cleared bits, and delete page delta +1. Map by checkpoint identity, apply A2 full-delete semantics only to the tdef churn fixture, and keep every value non-evidential
synthetic_input.arithmetic_rule: prove the D A/B/A/C record-set relation with regrowth strictly larger than first growth, growth-only and full-delete churn-only tdef transitions, and every analyzer checkpoint equality. No equality or count may depend on a hand-authored fixture constant
synthetic_input.record_uniqueness_rule: the decisive fixture must have at least 32 all-D-zero bytes after its last flipped global-map byte and the page-terminal byte-property tie-break must leave exactly one record; shorter equivalent endpoints must be generated and rejected
synthetic_input.base_discrimination_rule: the all-layers-decisive fixture must produce a slot-0 flip at H_REL_0064 that leaves exactly one base formula. A second valid fixture with no discriminating flip must retain decisive earlier global layers and report insufficient_base_discrimination only for extended_base
synthetic_input.inline_boundary_rule: generate empty, partial, and full anchor-fill variants with one invariant global-map inline boundary and recover the same boundary in all variants
synthetic_input.slot_rule: for conversion fixtures with one or two active slots, recover a decisive conversion layer when exactly two are active by H_REL_0904; zero at conversion and a final count other than two reach their exact named layer outcomes
synthetic_input.abort_reachability_rule: every Abort or early terminal has one stable predicate_registry mapping and a single named perturbation of a schedule-derived fixture that reaches the exact reason and layer; dead, unnamed, or unproducible sites fail the dry run

source_contract_checks: A2 code does not import, copy, or depend on A1 hand-typed fixture counts or a hard-coded A1 conversion checkpoint
every Abort has exactly one stable reason-to-predicate mapping and a schedule-derived reachability case
page qualification precedes interval enumeration and interval predicates use bounded O(1) prefix-difference queries
record and pointer exclusions are transition-structural and identical on every page; no page number or byte-offset blacklist exists
bytes commonly described as page headers receive no positional meaning and enter a record or pointer only if they satisfy the same transition signature as every other byte
global delimitation uses D only; conversion, slot, inline, polarity agreement, and base evaluation use L/P/H on the frozen global record; tdef carries only pointer predicates
both D polarities, slot counts 0/1/2, all conversion ordinals plus never, anchor fills, and record-end slack values are exercised
a schema-valid layered report with at least one decisive submodel passes validate-document and is accepted with bundle status decisive_pending_independent_validation
analyzer_dry_run_contract.acceptance_criteria: the retained-A1 report opens no holdout, stays within blob, page, candidate, and work ceilings, applies the exact projection table, resolves one global record end with slack, and emits the named legacy state. The synthetic report covers every parameter, layered and terminal case, recovers an all-layers-decisive model, retains partial outcomes, and records every predicate id. The decisive validator case must pass. Any missing case, hash, bound, mapping, assertion, or generator-produced equality keeps acquisition BLOCKED
analyzer_dry_run_contract.disclosure_rule: retain both schema-valid dry-run reports, fixtures, hashes, commands, exact commits, layered outcomes, predicate ids, and decisive-validator result and record them in an additive A2 provenance entry before acquisition; all are non-evidential

predicate_registry.reporting_rule: every Abort or early terminal attaches exactly one registered predicate id and its pinned reason to the applicable retained layer result; no unregistered or remapped Abort is permitted

layered_outcomes.global_map_record: decisive when one D-delimited record and one D-selected polarity survive derivation and predict the holdout; independent of later conversion, base, and tdef outcomes
layered_outcomes.global_map_conversion_inline: evaluated only on the frozen global record; decisive when one conversion, valid slot schedule, polarity cross-check, and inline boundary predict the holdout
layered_outcomes.global_map_extended_base: evaluated on the frozen global record and conversion; decisive when one base predicts holdout. Insufficient slot-0 discrimination is only this layer's no-outcome
layered_outcomes.tdef_pointer_pair: decisive when one separately delimited tdef record with one growth/churn pointer pair predicts holdout; independent of global conversion and base outcomes

decision_rules.freeze_rule: persist and hash every derivation candidate set and every layer result from replicas 1 and 2 before any replica-3 structural validation or page access; holdout cannot alter any layer
decision_rules.scientific_outcome: one_or_more_submodels_predict_holdout when at least one layer is decisive on holdout, otherwise no_submodel_predicts_holdout. An unmet layer never erases another layer's result
decision_rules.terminal_disambiguation: global and tdef searches each use distinct reasons for zero qualifying pages, multiple qualifying pages, zero records, and multiple records; record-end, polarity, conversion, slot, pointer, inline, base, campaign, and holdout failures retain their own mapped reasons

decisive_report_handling.campaign_behavior: a schema-valid layered report with one or more decisive holdout-predicting submodels completes the campaign successfully, is inventoried and retained, and must pass the A2 contract validator without being routed through an A1 validator or deletion path
decisive_report_handling.independent_validation_rule: structural validation accepts the retained layered result but capability verification remains not_independently_validated until a separately provenanced independent recomputing validator accepts the report and bundle

runtime_design.timing_derivation: post-PR-33 run 11 reached H_REL_0904 in 400.440-462.513 seconds with final idle costs 26.317-26.654 seconds; run 12 reached it in 543.107-619.412 seconds with final idle costs 35.394-35.901 seconds. The slow observed A2-equivalent prefix plus idle is 654.865 seconds. A 70.135-second allowance for D_RECREATE_EMPTY, full-delete differences, and rounding freezes the per-replica projection at 725 seconds
runtime_design.per_replica_headroom: the 2400-second worker ceiling is 3.31x the 725-second post-PR-33 projection
runtime_design.campaign_headroom: independent replicas run concurrently; 725 seconds plus the full 900-second fan-in safety bound yields a 1625-second complete-campaign estimate. The 2700-second campaign bound is 1.66x that estimate, and the estimate remains below the 1800-second hosted target
runtime_design.bounds_sanity_basis: run 12 observed 20,701 changed hash entries over 71 checkpoints versus the 65,536 bound; projected A2 logical reads are about 254 MiB versus 2 GiB; projected inserted rows are about 150,000 versus 524,288. Dry-run boundary cases must accept each exact ceiling and reject one over
